_: Copy this to capture.json and edit it. Nothing here is read unless
_1: capture.json exists -- video capture is OFF by default, and an
_2: installer never ships a live capture.json. Keys beginning with _ are
_3: ignored, so they can be used as comments in a format that has none.
_device: DirectShow name of the capture card, EXACTLY as ffmpeg lists
_device2: it. Run `doscap devices` -- it prints the block to paste here.
_device3: This is why the feature needs configuring rather than guessing:
_device4: the name belongs to one machine, and a shipped default would be
_audio: HDMI carries audio too, and on a DOS box that is the PC speaker
_audio2: and the AdLib. It is the only way to check MOZART, AMOZART or
_audio3: RAYCAST's music from another machine. null disables `rec --audio`.
_geometry: What to ask the card for. `doscap modes` lists what it can
_geometry2: actually do. 1600x1200 is 4:3, which is the shape a DOS box
_geometry3: puts out; a 16:9 capture mode letterboxes or stretches it.
_pixfmt: yuyv422 is uncompressed off the stick. mjpeg is the alternative
_pixfmt2: and costs less USB bandwidth, but it recompresses text badly --
_pixfmt3: which is most of what a DOS screen is.
_rtbufsize: NOT a tuning knob. One 1600x1200 yuyv422 frame is 3.84 MB and
_rtbufsize2: ffmpeg's default real-time buffer is about 3 MB -- less than a
_rtbufsize3: single frame -- so it drops frames immediately. Raise it with
_rtbufsize4: the resolution, not with the length of the recording.
_warmup: The first frame out of a capture device can be whatever was in
_warmup2: its buffer before we opened it, so a snapshot asks for several
_warmup3: and keeps the last. Costs warmup_frames/framerate seconds.
_preset: x264 speed. Measured on this hardware at 1600x1200x60:
_preset2: ultrafast held 60 fps with ZERO dropped frames; veryfast did
_preset3: not keep up and dropped them. If your capture drops frames, make
_preset4: this faster before you make anything else smaller.
_preview: `doscap live` settings. Sound is ON by default; --mute turns
_preview2: it off. audio_buffer_ms is how much audio the DEVICE buffers:
_preview3: too small starves the renderer and sounds choppy, too large
_preview4: lags the picture. 0 uses the device default.
_out_dir: Where shots and recordings land. Relative paths are resolved
_ffmpeg: Full paths, only if ffmpeg is not on PATH. A winget install is
_ffmpeg2: found automatically even before the shell has been restarted.
_open_timeout: Seconds to wait for the device to open before giving up.
_open_timeout2: A capture that cannot open must FAIL rather than wait:
_open_timeout3: everything in this project that ever needed hands on the
_open_timeout4: keyboard looked like a hang first.
